header.closeCompanyBody: The company is saved automatically. You will need the file password to open it again.

help.start: Create a new company, or open a company file you already have. Each company is one file on your computer, protected by its own password. You can copy the file to back it up or send it to your accountant.
help.wizard: Answer a few questions to set up your company. You can go back to any step. Nothing is created until the last step.
help.summary: This is your starting page. It shows your company and will show your key balances once you start recording entries.
help.settings: Choose the language, text size and number style. These settings are saved on this computer.
help.accounts: The chart of accounts is the list of accounts every entry is recorded against. Group accounts hold other accounts; only the accounts under them take entries. Add, rename or move accounts at any time. An account that already has entries cannot be deleted, but its entries can be moved to another account.
help.vouchers: Vouchers are your records of money coming in, going out, or being moved between accounts. A draft can be changed freely and does not affect your reports. Once you post a voucher it gets a number and appears in your books.
help.voucher: Fill in the date and the accounts, then save. "Save as draft" keeps your work without recording it. "Save and post" records it in your books and gives it a number. A posted voucher can still be corrected unless its month is locked.
help.reports: Every report is worked out from your posted vouchers. Click any amount in a report to see the entries behind it.
help.report: Choose the dates at the top. Click any amount to see the entries behind it. Use Export to print the report or save it as PDF, Excel or CSV.
help.parties: Customers owe you money and suppliers are owed money by you. Every entry on a receivable or payable account names the customer or supplier it is for, which is what lets Baba show each one's statement and how long their balance has been outstanding. A customer or supplier that has been used cannot be deleted, only switched off.
help.costCenters: A cost center (or project) is an optional tag you can put on any voucher line, for example a branch or a job. The profit and loss can then be read for each one.
help.transfer: A transfer moves money from one bank or cash account to another, for example taking cash to the bank. Choose where it comes from, where it goes and the amount. Nothing is earned or spent, so your profit does not change.
help.bank: These are your bank and cash accounts. Reconcile an account when you get the bank's statement: you check that what Baba has recorded matches what the bank says, line by line.
help.reconcile: Type the date and the closing balance from the bank's statement, then tick every entry that appears on it. When the difference is zero, finish. Entries that are not on the statement yet stay unticked for next time. If you load the statement from a file, Baba suggests the matches.
help.opening: The opening balances are what the business had on the day you start using Baba: cash, bank, what customers owe, what you owe, and the owners' capital. Debits and credits must be equal. There is only one opening-balances entry, and you can correct it later.
help.yearEnd: At the end of a fiscal year you close it. Baba moves the year's profit or loss into retained earnings, locks the year's months, and saves a copy of your file first. If you made a mistake you can reopen the latest closed year.
help.rates: For every foreign currency you use, enter how many units of your own currency it is worth, from a date on. A voucher or document in that currency starts from the latest rate on or before its date, and you can change it for that one document.
help.documents: Quotes, orders, delivery notes, invoices, and credit or debit notes. Quotes and orders post nothing. An invoice posts to the customer or supplier and to revenue or expenses when you issue it, and you can change or delete it later. Use "Turn this into" to move to the next document without typing it again.
help.products: Products and services you sell or buy, with their prices and accounts, and price lists that give chosen customers their own prices. Choosing a product on an invoice fills in its name, price and account.
help.recurring: Invoices and entries that Baba makes again by itself, such as monthly rent. Open an invoice or a journal entry and choose Repeat to set one up. When the app is opened, whatever came due is made: as drafts to check, or issued straight away if you chose that.
help.taxCodes: The tax codes you can put on invoice lines. The codes of your country come ready made with their rates; you choose which accounts they post to, which one new lines start with, and you can add your own. A line keeps the rate it was written with, so changing a code never changes an old invoice.
help.stock: What is in stock and what it is worth. Opening stock is what you already had when you started. A stock count compares what you counted with what is recorded and books only the difference. A transfer moves stock between warehouses without changing its value. Sales and purchase invoices move stock by themselves.
help.warehouses: Warehouses are the places where you keep stock. Every movement of stock names one. One warehouse is the default, and new documents use it unless you choose another.
help.assets: Your fixed assets (and intangible ones such as software) with their cost, depreciation and book value. Baba posts each month's depreciation by itself for the months that have ended, and you can run it up to any date. When you sell or scrap an asset, Baba takes it off the books and records the gain or loss.
help.employees: Your employees with their pay, the allowances and deductions they get, and their leave. Choose "National" for citizens of your country: the social insurance of your country applies to them as set in the payroll settings.
help.payroll: Each month has a payroll run: a payslip for every employee, worked out from their pay. Posting it records salaries, social insurance and deductions in your books; paying it takes the net salaries out of the bank. Once you have made the first month, later months are made (and posted) for you when you open the company. Change a payslip for overtime or a deduction, and the books follow.
help.claims: Expenses your employees paid for and want back. A claim is written, sent for approval, then approved or rejected. Approving it puts the expenses in your books and records that you owe the employee; paying it clears that. Choose the employee, then add a line for each receipt.
help.budgets: Plan what you expect to earn and spend: an amount for each revenue and expense account, month by month. Then open "Budget versus actual" to see how the year is going. Type a yearly total to spread it over twelve months, or change single months.

terms.fiscalYear: The 12-month period your accounts are totalled for. For most businesses it is the calendar year.
terms.baseCurrency: The main currency your books are kept in. Amounts in other currencies are converted into it.
terms.chartOfAccounts: The list of accounts (like Cash, Sales or Rent) that every entry is recorded against.
terms.taxRegistration: The number your tax authority gave your business. It is printed on your invoices.
terms.modules: Optional parts of Baba. Turn on only what you use. You can change this later.
terms.filePassword: Protects your company file. Without it nobody can read the file.

reports.title: Reports

descriptions.trial-balance: Every account with its debit and credit totals. The totals must be equal.
descriptions.profit-and-loss: Income less expenses for a period: how much you earned.
descriptions.balance-sheet: What you own, what you owe and what is left for the owners, on one day.
descriptions.statement-of-account: Every entry on one account with a running balance.
descriptions.general-ledger: The entries of every account, one account after another.
descriptions.journal: Every entry in date order, as it was recorded.
descriptions.party-statement: Every entry of one customer or supplier with a running balance.
descriptions.aging-receivable: Who owes you, and for how long it has been overdue.
descriptions.aging-payable: Whom you owe, and for how long it has been overdue.
descriptions.cost-centers: Revenue, expenses and profit of each cost center.
descriptions.tax-return: What was sold and bought under each tax code in a period, and the tax to pay or claim back.
descriptions.stock-valuation: What is in stock on a day and what it is worth. Checked against the stock accounts of the ledger.
descriptions.stock-movements: Every movement of stock in a period: what came in, what went out, and at what value.
descriptions.stock-reorder: Products whose stock has fallen to their reorder level.
descriptions.asset-register: Cost, depreciation so far and book value of every asset on a day, checked against the ledger.
descriptions.payroll-summary: Every payslip of the months in a period, with the bank details: also the list to give your bank.
descriptions.leave-balances: Annual leave each employee has earned, taken and has left.
descriptions.end-of-service: What each employee would be owed at the end of service, and whether your books hold that much.
descriptions.budget-vs-actual: What you planned for each revenue and expense account in a period, what really happened, and the difference.

reports.chooseAccountFirst: Choose an account to see its statement.
reports.choosePartyFirst: Choose a customer or supplier to see the statement.

bank.title: Bank and cash
bank.emptyBody: Mark an account as "Cash or bank" in the chart of accounts to see it here.
bank.statementBalanceHelp: The balance the bank prints at the end of the statement.
bank.differenceHelp: The ticked entries do not add up to the statement balance yet. Tick the entries that are on the statement, or check the balance you typed.

bank.nothingToCheck: Nothing left to check up to this date.
bank.entriesUpTo: {{count}} entries up to the statement date

bank.undoBody: Its entries become unchecked again and can be changed. You can reconcile again afterwards.

reconciliation.none-to-undo: There is no reconciliation to undo.

bank.account-invalid: This is not a bank or cash account.

yearEnd.title: Year-end
yearEnd.intro: Closing a year puts its profit or loss into retained earnings, locks its months, and saves a copy of your file first. Do it after the year has ended and everything is posted.
yearEnd.stepProfit: bring the year's revenue and expense accounts to zero and put the profit or loss into retained earnings,
yearEnd.stepLock: lock the twelve months of the year, so nothing can be added to them,
yearEnd.stepBackup: save a copy of your company file next to it, from just before the close.
yearEnd.canReopen: You can reopen the year afterwards if you find a mistake.
yearEnd.closedBody: The closing entry is {{number}}. A copy of the file from before the close was saved as {{path}}.
yearEnd.confirmReopenBody: The closing entry is deleted and the months of the year are unlocked, so vouchers can be changed again. Close the year again when you are done.

year.not-ended: This year has not ended yet.
year.drafts-exist: There are draft vouchers in this year. Post or delete them first.
year.no-retained-earnings: There is no retained earnings account. Mark an equity account as "Retained earnings" in the chart of accounts.
year.nothing-to-close: This year has no revenue or expenses to close.
year.later-year-closed: A later year is closed. Reopen the latest closed year first.

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: A backup is a complete copy of your company in one file, protected by the same password.
backups.automaticUpdate: Baba saves a copy automatically before it updates your file to a newer version.
backups.automaticYearEnd: Baba saves a copy automatically before closing a fiscal year.
backups.restore: To go back to a backup, use "Restore a backup" on the start screen (close the company first).

import.partiesIntro: Add them from a CSV or Excel file. The first row names the columns. Only the name is needed; codes are filled in for you.
import.skipped: {{count}} lines were already there and were skipped.
import.failed: Nothing was imported. Fix these rows and choose the file again:

import.unreadable: The file could not be read. Use a CSV or an Excel (.xlsx) file.
import.empty: The file has no rows to import.

statement.amount-column-missing: There is no Amount column (or Debit and Credit columns).
statement.amount-invalid: The amount is missing or not a number.

account.type-unknown: The type is not one of Asset, Liability, Equity, Revenue, Expense.
account.role-unknown: The special use is not known.

party.kind-unknown: The kind must be customer or supplier.
party.credit-limit-invalid: The credit limit is not a number.

import.productsIntro: Add products and services from a CSV or Excel file. The first row names the columns. Only one name is needed; a missing code is filled in. Accounts and tax codes are written as their codes.
import.ratesIntro: Add rates from a CSV or Excel file: the currency, the date it applies from, and what one unit is worth in your currency. A rate for a date that already has one replaces it.
import.journalIntro: Post journal entries from a CSV or Excel file. Rows with the same Entry number make one entry, which must balance. Accounts, customers, suppliers and cost centers are written as their codes. If anything is wrong nothing is posted.
import.openingIntro: Add the opening balances from a CSV or Excel file with an account and a debit or a credit on each row. It becomes the one opening-balances entry, dated the day before your books start, and it must balance.

trade.emptyPriceListsBody: A price list gives chosen customers their own prices. Give it to a customer on their page.
trade.productAccountHelp: Used when a document line has no account of its own.
trade.priceListCurrencyHelp: The list is used on documents in this currency.
trade.priceListHelp: This customer gets the prices of this list on documents in its currency.

document.party-wrong-kind: This is not the right kind of customer or supplier for this document.
document.party-inactive: This customer or supplier is switched off.
document.discount-invalid: The discount must be between 0 and 100.
document.kind-cannot-change: A document cannot change into another kind. Use Turn this into.
document.not-draft: Only a draft can be saved as a draft.
document.converted: This document was already turned into another one.
document.not-issued: Issue the document before turning it into another one.
document.cannot-convert: This document cannot be turned into that.
document.total-not-positive: The total must be more than zero.
document.control-account-missing: There is no active customers or suppliers account to post to. Check the chart of accounts.
document.has-payments: This invoice has a payment against it. Delete the receipt or payment first.
document.has-notes: This invoice has a credit or debit note. Delete the note first.
document.immutable: Under the e-invoicing rules of your country an issued invoice cannot be changed or deleted. Make a credit note instead.

line.discount-invalid: The discount must be between 0 and 100.
line.cost-center-unknown: That cost center no longer exists.
line.account-invalid: Choose an account that is active and takes entries.
line.account-required: Choose the account this line posts to.
line.tax-code-unknown: That tax code no longer exists.
line.tax-code-inactive: That tax code is switched off.
line.tax-code-not-effective: That tax code does not apply on the date of this document.
line.tax-account-missing: This tax code has no account to post its tax to. Choose one in Tax codes.

product.code-duplicate: Another product already uses this code.
product.account-invalid: Choose an account that is active and takes entries.
product.in-use: This product is on a document, so it cannot be deleted. Switch it off instead.
product.tax-code-unknown: That tax code no longer exists.
product.barcode-duplicate: Another product already has this barcode.
product.reorder-negative: The reorder level cannot be negative.
product.has-stock: Stock has been recorded for this product, so it must stay a stock item.

price-list.product-unknown: A product on the list no longer exists.
price-list.product-twice: A product can be on the list only once.
price-list.in-use: A customer uses this price list. Choose another for them first, or switch it off.

settlement.document-unavailable: That invoice is not open for payment any more.
settlement.amount-too-high: The amount is more than what is outstanding on the invoice.
settlement.nothing-to-settle: Type an amount for at least one invoice, or an extra amount.
settlement.mixed-currencies: Invoices in different currencies cannot be paid together.
settlement.currency-mismatch: The payment must be in the currency of the invoices.

fx.account-required: Add an active exchange-differences account to the chart of accounts first, so the gain or loss can be booked.

stock.insufficient: There is not enough stock for this quantity.
stock.would-leave-later-sales-short: Later sales need this stock. Change or delete them first.
stock.locked-period: This would change the cost of sales in a month that is locked.
stock.accounts-missing: The stock or cost of sales account is missing. Add it to the chart of accounts or choose one on the product.
stock.counter-account-missing: The stock gains and losses account is missing. Add it to the chart of accounts or choose an account.

trade.settlementNote: Type how much of each invoice this money pays. If the exchange rate changed since the invoices were issued, the gain or loss is booked for you.
trade.onAccountHelp: An advance that stays on the account until an invoice uses it.
trade.nothingOutstandingBody: There are no unpaid invoices in {{currency}}. Choose another currency, or type an amount below to keep it on account.
trade.settledNote: This invoice has been paid or credited, so it cannot be changed. Delete the receipt, payment or credit note first.
trade.productTaxHelp: Lines of this product start with this tax code.
trade.immutableNote: Under the e-invoicing rules of your country this invoice cannot be changed or deleted once it is issued. To correct it, make a credit note from it.

recurring.title: Recurring invoices and entries
recurring.intro: Baba keeps a copy of this as it is now and makes a new one each time it is due.
recurring.name: Name
recurring.autoIssueHelp: If this is off, each one is left as a draft for you to check and issue.
recurring.deleteBody: The schedule is deleted. Everything it already made stays.
recurring.ranOnOpen: {{count}} recurring invoices or entries were made. See Recurring.
recurring.emptyBody: Open an invoice or a journal entry and choose Repeat to make it again every week, month, quarter or year.
recurring.repeatHelp: Make this again on a schedule.
recurring.saved: The schedule was saved. See Recurring.

recurring.end-before-next: The last date cannot be before the next date.
recurring.template-unavailable: Baba makes this entry itself, so it cannot be repeated.

tax.title: Tax codes
tax.intro: Tax is added to each invoice line from its tax code and posted to the accounts shown here.
tax.rateHelp: Only a standard code has a rate.
tax.outputAccountHelp: Tax collected on sales is posted here.
tax.inputAccountHelp: Tax paid on purchases is posted here and claimed back.
tax.emptyBody: Your country has no tax codes. You can add your own with New tax code.
tax.packNote: This code came with your country. Its rate, treatment and dates are fixed; you can change its name and accounts.

tax.code-duplicate: Another tax code already uses this code.
tax.rate-invalid: The rate must be between 0 and 100.
tax.dates-invalid: The end date cannot be before the start date.
tax.account-invalid: Choose an active account of the right kind: a liability for tax payable, an asset for tax receivable.
tax.in-use: This tax code is used on a document or a product, so it cannot be deleted. Switch it off instead.
tax.pack-code: This code came with your country and cannot be deleted. Switch it off instead.
tax.inactive: Switch the code on before making it the default.

inventory.emptyWarehousesBody: A main warehouse is made for you the first time stock is recorded. Add others to keep stock in several places.
inventory.importIntro: Upload an Excel or CSV file with one row per product and warehouse. The whole file is rejected if any row has a problem, so nothing is half imported.

intro.Opening: The stock you already had when you started, with what each unit cost. It is posted against the account below.
intro.Adjustment: Count the stock, or enter the change directly. Only the difference from what is recorded is booked, to the account below.
intro.Transfer: Move stock from one warehouse to another. Its value does not change, so nothing is posted to the books.

inventory.counterAccountHelp: Leave empty to use the stock gains and losses account.
inventory.loadStock: Load the stock of this warehouse
inventory.unitCostHelp: Leave the cost empty for stock that is found in a count: it comes in at the current average cost.
inventory.nothingCounted: Nothing differs from what is recorded, so there is nothing to book.
inventory.emptyStockBody: Mark a product as a stock item, then record opening stock or buy it on a purchase invoice.
inventory.emptyDocumentsBody: Opening stock, counts and transfers you record appear here.
inventory.deleteDocumentBody: The stock goes back to how it was, and the entry it made in the books is removed.
inventory.stockItemHelp: Switch on to keep track of how many you have. Services are not stock items.
inventory.reorderLevelHelp: Baba warns you when the stock falls to this quantity. Leave 0 for no warning.
inventory.stockAccountHelp: Leave empty to use the company's stock account.
inventory.costOfSalesAccountHelp: Leave empty to use the company's cost of sales account.

warehouse.code-duplicate: Another warehouse already uses this code.
warehouse.in-use: Stock has moved through this warehouse, so it cannot be deleted. Switch it off instead.
warehouse.last-one: There must always be one active warehouse, and it must be the default.
warehouse.inactive: A warehouse that is switched off cannot be the default.

stockdoc.counter-account-invalid: Choose an active account that takes entries.
stockdoc.kind-cannot-change: The type of a stock document cannot be changed.
stockdoc.product-not-stock: Choose a product that is a stock item.
stockdoc.quantity-positive: The quantity must be more than zero.
stockdoc.same-warehouse: Choose a different warehouse to move the stock to.

assets.title: Fixed assets
assets.undone: The latest month of depreciation was taken back.
assets.importIntro: Upload an Excel or CSV file with one row per asset. The whole file is rejected if any row has a problem. Assets already in use can say how much they have been depreciated so far.
assets.runIntro: Depreciation is posted for every month up to and including the month of this date that is not done yet.
assets.ranOnOpen: Depreciation was posted for {{count}} months that had ended.
assets.emptyBody: Add the things you own that last for years, such as equipment, vehicles or software, and Baba will depreciate them every month.
assets.disposeIntro: Depreciation is brought up to the month of this date, then the asset leaves the books. What you receive, less its book value, is the gain or loss.
assets.gainLossHelp: Leave empty to use the gain or loss on disposal account.
assets.salvageHelp: What it should be worth at the end of its life. It is never depreciated below this.
assets.annualRateHelp: A share of what is left, taken every month.
assets.assetAccountHelp: The account that holds its cost, where the purchase was posted.
assets.defaultAccountHelp: Leave empty to use the account made for this.
assets.alreadyInUse: Already in use before you started with Baba? Say how much has been depreciated so far, and up to which month.
assets.depreciatedThroughHelp: Any date in the last month already depreciated.
assets.lockedNote: Depreciation has been posted for this asset, so what it was worked out from cannot change. You can still change its name, cost center and notes.

asset.code-duplicate: Another asset already uses this code.
asset.cost-center-unknown: That cost center no longer exists.
asset.account-invalid: Choose an active account that takes entries and fits (asset accounts for the cost and the depreciation, an expense account for the expense).
asset.accounts-same: The depreciation account must differ from the asset account.
asset.date-required: Enter the date it was acquired.
asset.cost-invalid: The cost must be more than zero.
asset.salvage-invalid: The salvage value must be zero or more, and less than the cost.
asset.life-invalid: Enter the useful life in months (more than zero).
asset.rate-invalid: The yearly rate must be above 0 and at most 100.
asset.opening-invalid: Depreciation so far cannot be more than the cost less the salvage value.
asset.terms-locked: Depreciation has been posted, so the cost, dates, method and accounts cannot change.
asset.in-use: This asset has depreciation or was disposed of, so it cannot be deleted.
asset.nothing-to-undo: There is no depreciation to take back.
asset.disposed-since: An asset was disposed of in that month or later, so its depreciation cannot be taken back.
asset.already-disposed: This asset was already disposed of.
asset.disposal-before-acquisition: The disposal cannot be before the asset was acquired.
asset.proceeds-invalid: The amount received cannot be negative.
asset.disposal-account-missing: Choose the account for the gain or loss.
asset.not-disposed: This asset has not been disposed of.

employees.title: Employees
employees.importIntro: Upload an Excel or CSV file with one row per employee. The whole file is rejected if any row has a problem. Allowances and deductions are given to each employee afterwards.
employees.emptyBody: Add your employees with their basic salary, and Baba will work out their payslips every month.
employees.isNationalHelp: A citizen of the company's country: the insurance scheme for nationals applies.
employees.leaveDateHelp: Fill in when the employee leaves. Pay stops after this day.
employees.componentValueHelp: A fixed amount a month, or a percentage of the basic salary, as the allowance or deduction is set up.
employees.leaveBroughtForwardHelp: Days of leave left on the date below. More is earned each month after it.
employees.leaveDaysHelp: Leave empty to count every day from the first to the last.
employees.emptyLeaveBody: Record the leave employees take, and their balance follows.
employees.componentsIntro: The kinds of allowance (housing, transport) and deduction (loan repayment) you give employees. Choose them on each employee with their own amount.
employees.emptyComponentsBody: Add the kinds you use, such as a housing allowance.
employees.defaultValueHelp: Each employee can have their own.
employees.deductionAccountHelp: Required: for example the loans account for a loan repayment.
employees.earningAccountHelp: Leave empty to charge it to salaries.
employees.insurableHelp: Switch on if the insurance is worked out on this too (housing usually).
employees.inEndOfServiceHelp: Switch on if the end-of-service gratuity is worked out on this too.

employee.code-duplicate: Another employee already uses this code.
employee.join-required: Enter the date the employee joined.
employee.leave-before-join: The last day of work cannot be before the joining date.
employee.basic-invalid: The basic salary cannot be negative.
employee.leave-days-invalid: Annual leave must be between 0 and 366 days.
employee.cost-center-unknown: That cost center no longer exists.
employee.component-unknown: Choose an allowance or deduction that exists and is on.
employee.component-twice: This allowance or deduction is given twice.
employee.in-use: This employee has payslips or leave, so they cannot be deleted. Switch them off instead.

component.code-duplicate: Another one already uses this code.
component.value-invalid: The amount cannot be negative, and a percentage cannot be over 1,000.
component.account-required: Choose the account the deduction goes to.
component.account-invalid: Choose an active account that takes entries.
component.in-use: This is given to employees or on payslips, so it cannot be deleted. Switch it off instead.

leave.dates-invalid: The last day cannot be before the first.
leave.days-invalid: The days must be more than zero.

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.startHint: Start with the first month you want Baba to run. From then on, every month that ends is made for you when you open the company.
payroll.emptyBody: Add your employees first, then make the first month. Baba works out each payslip and the social insurance.
payroll.newMonthIntro: A payslip is made for every employee who worked that month, from their current pay. You can change them before posting.
payroll.provisionAlreadyRight: The provision already matches what is owed.
payroll.noEndOfService: This country has no end-of-service gratuity, so there is nothing to set aside.
payroll.endOfServiceIntro: What each employee would be owed if their service ended at the end of last month. The provision in your books is brought to this amount once a month.
payroll.provisionFor: Post the provision for the month of
payroll.postedNote: This month is in your books. If you change a payslip, the books follow.
payroll.editPayslipHelp: Change an amount, or add a line such as overtime or a penalty. The social insurance is worked out again on the lines that count for it.
payroll.payIntro: The net salaries of this month are paid out of the account below, and what was owed to the employees is cleared.
payroll.ranOnOpen: Payroll was made for {{count}} months that had ended.
payroll.autoPostHelp: When on, a month that ends is made and posted when you open the company. You can still correct it afterwards. When off, it is made as a draft for you to check.
payroll.insuranceIntro: Started from {{name}}. Rates and limits change, so check them with the authority and correct them here.
payroll.insuranceNone: No social insurance is set up for this country. Enter rates below if your employees are insured.
payroll.insuranceFloorHelp: A lower wage is charged as if it were this.
payroll.insuranceCeilingHelp: Pay above this is not charged.

payroll.run-exists: This month already has a payroll.
payroll.no-employees: There is no employee to pay in that month.
payroll.not-draft: Only a draft can be made again.
payroll.paid: This month has been paid. Take the payment back first.
payroll.not-posted: Post the month to the books before paying it.
payroll.not-paid: This month has not been paid.
payroll.cash-account-invalid: Choose a bank or cash account to pay from.
payroll.accounts-missing: Payroll accounts are missing. Choose them in the payroll settings.
payroll.nothing-to-pay: There is no net pay to pay out.
payroll.net-negative: A payslip has deductions larger than the pay. Change it first.
payroll.eos-done: The provision for that month was already posted.
payroll.eos-not-applicable: This country has no end-of-service gratuity.
payroll.eos-nothing-to-undo: There is no provision to take back.
payroll.percent-invalid: A percentage must be between 0 and 100.
payroll.limits-invalid: The lowest wage cannot be above the highest.
payroll.account-invalid: Choose an active account of the right kind that takes entries.

payslip.label-required: Enter a description for the line.
payslip.account-invalid: Choose an active account that takes entries.
payslip.account-required: A deduction needs the account it goes to.

claims.title: Expense claims
claims.emptyBody: When an employee pays for something for the business, write it here and send it for approval.
claims.intro: Add a line for each receipt. Nothing reaches your books until the claim is approved.

claim.account-invalid: Choose an active expense account that takes entries.
claim.amount-invalid: The amount must be more than zero.
claim.cost-center-unknown: That cost center no longer exists.
claim.not-draft: Only a draft or rejected claim can be changed or deleted.
claim.not-submitted: The claim has to be waiting for approval.
claim.not-approved: The claim has to be approved first.
claim.paid: This claim has been paid. Take the payment back first.
claim.not-paid: This claim has not been paid.
claim.cash-account-invalid: Choose a bank or cash account to pay from.
claim.accounts-missing: There is no account for expense claims payable. Give one account that special use in the chart of accounts.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.importIntro: Upload an Excel or CSV file with one row per account: the account code and the twelve months (headed 1 to 12), or a yearly total that is spread evenly. It replaces the budget shown.
budgets.copyIntro: Start from another year's budget, raised or lowered by a percentage. It replaces what is there now.
budgets.intro: Type an amount for any month, or a yearly total to spread it over the twelve months. Revenue and expense accounts only.

budget.cost-center-unknown: That cost center no longer exists.
budget.account-invalid: Only revenue and expense accounts that take entries can be budgeted.
budget.account-twice: This account is in the budget twice.
budget.months-invalid: An account needs an amount for each of the twelve months.
budget.nothing-to-copy: There is no budget in that year to copy.
budget.account-column-missing: The file needs an Account code column.
budget.amounts-missing: The file needs month columns (1 to 12) or a Yearly total column.
budget.account-unknown: No revenue or expense account has this code.
budget.amount-invalid: The amount must be a number, zero or more.
